pure-announcement.rationale: It is architecture documentation for an identity system, not a launch or release note — the mechanisms described transfer beyond the Google product.

duplicate.rationale: mcp-authorization-hardening covers OAuth alignment at the MCP protocol level, not per-agent SPIFFE workload identity, certificate-bound tokens, or the credential-broker pattern this note centres on.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Every claim is checkable against Google Cloud's published docs and the open SPIFFE specification the identity format builds on.

durability.rationale: The load-bearing content — SPIFFE-based per-agent identity instead of shared service accounts, mTLS+DPoP double-bound tokens that cannot be replayed, and a broker that keeps raw end-user credentials out of the agent — is standards-grounded security architecture that will hold in twelve months regardless of Google's product surface.

actionability.rationale: A reader designing agent authentication can act on the pattern directly: attested identity per agent, tokens bound to certificates, outbound credentials brokered by auth model (3LO user-delegated vs 2LO machine-to-machine vs vaulted API keys).

atomicity.rationale: The identity format, token binding, and credential brokering are facets of one coherent idea — strongly attested per-agent identity with unreplayable, never-exposed credentials — stateable in a single paragraph.
